clue.text: Fire past island as military horseman

indicators.note: past means the word for island comes before, going past it to the next piece

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A soldier on horseback opens fire after passing an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like gunfire, which suits a soldier, but here it means dismissal from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cossacks were famed cavalry of the Russian steppes, so one is a mounted soldier.

clue.text: Cooking ingredient, exquisite starter put in mouth: say, duck

indicators.note: put in signals that the starter goes inside the mouth word

parts.note: the mouth is an example of an organ, which the 'say' flags

indicators.note: starter means just the opening letter of the word exquisite is used

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: add a fine starter to the mouth, then the duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets E inside ORGAN to give OREGAN, then O follows. 'duck' wants to be the bird in a recipe; it is a cricket score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb is a common seasoning in Mediterranean dishes, so it is something cooks add to food.

clue.text: Paul's stage opening — there's my cue!

definitions.note: the clue means the surname belonging to Paul, the singer-songwriter

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word stage

parts.note: an actor hearing the cue would say I'm on

explanation.surface: A performer hears the line that sends them on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is himself Paul, adding a wink; the def is the surname of Paul of the singing duo in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Simon is the songwriter half of the 1960s folk duo, so his surname belongs to that Paul.

indicators.note: disheartening removes the heart, leaving only the outer letters of the word cute

parts.note: cilia are eyelashes in anatomical terms

explanation.surface: A girl's cute lashes are, oddly, disheartening.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 and 15' point to the entries naming the duo: CECILIA is one of their hit songs about a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The duo's 1970 hit song is named after and addressed to a girl of this name.

parts.note: Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone describes a boy-girl pairing standing beside the duo.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference: a song written and recorded by the duo in 3 and 15.
explanation.definitionFit: The duo released a well-known song of this title on the album Bookends.

indicators.note: glugging means swallowing, so the wine word takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: Mosel is a German white wine named after its river region

explanation.surface: Someone samples wine while gulping down river water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glugging' sets R inside MOSEL. 'Taste' looks like a verb but is a noun, a small bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste of something is a small mouthful of it, a little sample or bite.

indicators.note: ground as in milled or crushed, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A family member's land, or their estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' and 'grounds' look like the same word twice; the first is the anagram signal, the second the definition (reasons).
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds for a decision are the reasons behind it, its underlying logic.

clue.text: Crowns on top of aristocracy, breaking heart

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the heart word open so the other letters go inside

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
taken as written

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word aristocracy

explanation.surface: Coronets sit on the heads of nobles, breaking hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts ONA inside CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corona is Latin for crown, and in English names crown-like halos or circles.

clue.text: Useless effort debated without value in existence

indicators.note: useless suggests the words are no good as they stand and must be remade

explanation.surface: A discussion that went nowhere is judged a waste of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Useless' looks like the definition but signals the rearrangement of EFFORT DEBATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone would be better dead means their living has no worth, an idiom of despair.

definitions.meaning: short for permutation, a mathematical arrangement or combination
a chemically set curly hairstyle, locks being hair

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both short for permutation and the name of a curled hairstyle.

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: made of terry, the towelling fabric
a chart is a plan or diagram

explanation.surface: A dessert turns out to be a fabricated scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A towelling CHART becomes a CHERRY TART when the openings swap. 'fabricated' looks like 'made up' but means made of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A pudding of fruit in pastry is a dessert, which British English calls a sweet.

indicators.note: in places the ending letter inside the passage word

parts.note: a canal is a passage or channel

indicators.note: ending means the last letter of the word ardour

explanation.surface: A passionate person's desire ends up in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside CANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal desires are bodily and fleshly, appealing to the senses.

parts.note: a song by the duo, whose title also describes peace, as quiet is what you hear in calm

explanation.definitionFit: The duo's famous song title also describes tranquillity, which sounds like a piece of their work.

clue.text: Girl has no bananas for Persians, perhaps

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A girl with no bananas swaps them for cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but signals the rearrangement. Persians here are cats, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Persian cats are a breed with long fur, so they are examples of long-furred cats.

clue.text: Art dealer's conclusion: jazzy stuff collected by highlander

indicators.note: collected by means held inside the highlander word

parts.note: a Gael is a Scottish highlander

indicators.note: conclusion means the last letter of the word dealer

parts.note: funk is a jazzy, rhythmic style of music

explanation.surface: An art dealer ends up with jazz records gathered by a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected by' puts RFUNK inside GAEL. 'Art' looks like painting but is the first name of the duo's other member.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Garfunkel is the singer who partnered Paul in the duo, so his surname follows the first name.

clue.text: Old place for shopping bag, or all boxes

indicators.note: boxes means contains, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: Advice about packing a bag, perhaps with every item in boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like a noun but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the agora was the public square where the market was held.

parts.note: German is a nationality

explanation.surface: Someone decides which nationality, English, is suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or pertinent to the matter at hand.

clue.text: I note well, plant has to develop internally

parts.note: NB stands for nota bene, Latin for note well
a reed is a waterside plant

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a plant must grow inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note well' looks like a separate instruction; it is NB.
explanation.definitionFit: To inbreed is to mate within a closed group, so a line develops from within itself.

clue.text: Most secretive, a US soldier's incest?

annotationWithheld.why: Most secretive, a US soldier's incest? (7): A GI is in CEST, so 'incest' gives both the container indicator 'in' and the outer letters CEST, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Most secretive, a US soldier's incest?

parts.note: a lotto is a lottery drawing lucky numbers

explanation.surface: A billion spent on lottery tickets is money down the drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' looks like squandered but is slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, which is also what wasted means as slang.

clue.text: Journalist stealing public money in West Country town, by 3 and 15

indicators.note: in places the journalist group inside the town

parts.note: Bridgwater is a town in Somerset, in the West Country of England

indicators.note: stealing means taking the other pieces inside

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a crossword staple for a journalist
overt means public, done openly
the rouble is Russian money

explanation.surface: A reporter embezzles public funds in a Somerset town, alongside the duo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public money' reads as one idea, state funds, but splits into two words. The town is spelt with no E after the G; it is in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The duo's best-selling album and title song, released in 1970.

clue.text: I duck at the first attempt

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of none

explanation.surface: Someone ducks at their first try.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in one means managing it with a single go, without retrying.

parts.note: a basket and a case are both containers
a basket and a case are both containers

explanation.surface: A ruined thing is just a pair of boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' is a person who cannot cope, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is slang for someone too stressed to function, a nervous wreck.

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the composer's name is dropped

parts.note: Irving Berlin was an American songwriter
OZ, an ounce, is a light unit of weight

explanation.surface: One composer's colleague is not completely a lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops N from BERLIN, giving BERLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer of the Symphonie fantastique.

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being worked on and changed

explanation.surface: A hungry person thinks of food while breaking for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' is a commercial break on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Commercials fill the breaks in television programmes, so they are items in a break.
